svg.title: Set-Aside and SLED Bid Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-set-aside-sled-bid-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Set-Aside and SLED Bid Gates; subtitle: Four checks before spending time on a certification or a bid; caption: Neil McDonnell counts 11,152 FY2023 SDVOSB set-aside awards against 5,413,622 total new contract actions (WOSB 2,845, HUBZone 1,534, 8(a) 872), and reports that 20-30 sources-sought responses yield 5-10 RFP responses.; assumptions note: SLED figures come from separate speakers. Texas SmartBuy drops from 20,000 pages to 27 with status set to posted (SamSearch), and Foley Equipment estimates cooperative purchasing at about 20-30% of US purchases.; note: Sources - GovKidMethod (nRXCetmIWUs, xXM1cyLQ_jY), D'S Construction (yxjYYFbCa5E), Government Contracting Strategist & Host (iTD46ZpHbdI), GovClose | DoD Contract Academy (Qij-5QQmwc8), Neil McDonnell (4poj2n7iLrs).; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does the SAM set-aside filter on your NAICS code show enough set-aside volume to justify a certification?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold off on the certification, because the SBA is not going to be bringing you contracts (GovKidMethod).; gate: G2; question: Is there a mandatory pre-bid meeting, and can you attend it?; pass next: G3; fail action: Skip the bid, because missing it means you cannot submit (D'S Construction).; gate: G3; question: Have you pulled the bid tabs and the last award letter?; pass next: G4; fail action: Pull them and price against history instead of guessing (Government Contracting Strategist & Host).; gate: G4; question: Did your questions go in at the sources-sought or RFI stage?; pass next: Bid, and keep flooding sources sought with a 10-20 firm team (Neil McDonnell); fail action: Target the next sources-sought notice, since contracting officers avoid one-on-one questions once a solicitation drops (GovClose).

circle.title: gate: G1; question: Does the SAM set-aside filter on your NAICS code show enough set-aside volume to justify a certification?; pass next: G2; fail action: Hold off on the certification, because the SBA is not going to be bringing you contracts (GovKidMethod).
gate: G2; question: Is there a mandatory pre-bid meeting, and can you attend it?; pass next: G3; fail action: Skip the bid, because missing it means you cannot submit (D'S Construction).

gate: G3; question: Have you pulled the bid tabs and the last award letter?; pass next: G4; fail action: Pull them and price against history instead of guessing (Government Contracting Strategist & Host).

gate: G4; question: Did your questions go in at the sources-sought or RFI stage?; pass next: Bid, and keep flooding sources sought with a 10-20 firm team (Neil McDonnell); fail action: Target the next sources-sought notice, since contracting officers avoid one-on-one questions once a solicitation drops (GovClose).

text.title: Assumptions: SLED figures come from separate speakers. Texas SmartBuy drops from 20,000 pages to 27 with status set to posted (SamSearch), and Foley Equipment estimates cooperative purchasing at about 20-30% of US purchases.
